description:
Section F — logging output safety, preventive hygiene. The crate currently emits ZERO `tracing::*` / `log::*` calls (verified by `grep -rn 'tracing\|log::\|info!\|debug!\|warn!\|error!' src/ tests/` returning empty). That is the right baseline.

The workspace has an established log-redaction canary pattern for crates that handle sensitive data, documented in workspace AGENTS.md 'Security testing' §2 and demonstrated in:
- `crate-jmap-base-client/tests/log_redaction.rs` — canary test
- `crate-jmap-base-client/tests/common/log_capture.rs` — reusable harness

What goes wrong if this stays as-is:
A future contributor adds a debug log statement like `tracing::info!(record = ?stored_obj, 'created');` to `MemoryBackend::create_object` or to a future production-backed `MetadataBackend`. The `Metadata::Annotation` variant carries vendor-specific private content in its `.extra` flatten map (per draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §1.2.1 the `maySetPrivate` gating exists precisely because this content is per-user-private). `{stored_obj:?}` interpolates the full `.extra` map via the derived `Debug` impl. The private vendor data — which may include workflow state, comments, decryption hints, or anything the spec permits a client to store — leaks to logs at the level the contributor chose.

Concrete attack scenarios this prevents:
1. A debug-logging refactor merged in a hurry interpolates `Metadata` Debug into a structured-logging field. Log aggregator stores the field. `isPrivate: true` annotations now exist in plaintext in centralised logs.
2. A panic message during a stuck migration includes the offending record. Panic backtrace + record content reach the crash reporter, which ships to a third-party SaaS.
3. An error variant interpolated via `Display` or `Debug` carries the description string from `SetError::with_description(format!(...meta...))` (already present at memory.rs:925, 935-936 for non-private uniqueness fields — but a future variant could include a private property name or value).

The canary test pattern installs a thread-local buffering tracing subscriber, exercises the code paths a future instrumenter would write, and asserts a canary literal does not appear in the captured output. The test exists BEFORE instrumentation is added so that the first contributor to add `tracing::*` discovers the canary failing in CI rather than shipping the leak.

What to file (P3 work bead, not part of this review):
- Add `crate-jmap-metadata-server/tests/log_redaction.rs` mirroring the base-client harness.
- Canary: store an `Annotation` with `.extra` value "REDACTION-CANARY-METADATA-826m" and exercise `/get`, `/changes`, `/set` create/update/destroy paths with a buffering subscriber. Assert the canary literal does not appear.
- Re-use `crate-jmap-base-client/tests/common/log_capture.rs` as the harness (copy-vendor rather than cross-crate import — base-client is the canonical pattern, not a public dependency).

Canonical-template note: `jmap-mail-server` does NOT have a log-redaction canary either (verified by `ls crate-jmap-mail-server/tests/`). Per workspace AGENTS.md propagation rule, add the canary to the canonical first if a workspace-wide sweep is desired; or accept this finding as metadata-server-specific because `isPrivate` content has a stronger spec-level confidentiality contract than Email body content (which is plainly visible to every authorised reader of an Email anyway).

Refs:
- workspace AGENTS.md 'Security testing' §2
- crate-jmap-base-client/tests/log_redaction.rs (reference pattern)
- crate-jmap-base-client/tests/common/log_capture.rs (reference harness)
- draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §1.2.1 (maySetPrivate gating — the spec-level confidentiality contract for the .extra content)
title: No log-redaction canary test for future tracing instrumentation that could leak Metadata.isPrivate content
